findings.title: Grafana branch in FilterView omits React key
findings.body: In FilterView.tsx the list maps rules to components with a computed `key`, but the `grafana` case returns `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` without `key={key}` while the `datasource` and unknown cases pass it. Missing keys cause React warnings and incorrect reconciliation during infinite scroll and filter updates, so state, focus, or action menus can attach to the wrong rule row.

findings.title: View link drops returnTo navigation context
findings.body: The old GrafanaRuleLoader built the rule view href with `createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new GrafanaRuleListItem builds `href` as `/alerting/grafana/<uid>/view` with no `returnTo`. Users opening a rule from the list lose the back-navigation context, so returning from the detail view no longer restores the list/filter state.

findings.title: Pause action can never show in ruler-less list view
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu computes `canPause` as ruler-ability OR grafana-prom-ability to support the list view without ruler data, but the Pause menu item still requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`. In the new list view `rulerRule` is undefined because ruler requests were removed, so the condition is always false and Pause never renders even when the prom-based ability says the user can pause.

findings.title: Delete action can never show in ruler-less list view
findings.body: AlertRuleMenu computes `canDelete` via ruler OR grafana-prom abilities, but the Delete menu item is guarded by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so Delete is never rendered for Grafana rules even for users with delete permission. The delete flow in RuleActionsButtons only needs an identifier from prom data, so gating on rulerRule is an unnecessary regression that removes delete from the list.

findings.title: Silence drawer never opens without rulerRule
findings.body: RuleActionsButtons shows a Silence menu item based on prom-based abilities, and clicking it sets `showSilenceDrawer`. The drawer itself is rendered only if `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` where `rule` is the optional ruler rule. In the list view only `promRule` is passed, so the predicate is false and `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` never mounts. Users see Silence but clicking it does nothing.

findings.title: Skipped grafana ability grants Duplicate to cloud rules
findings.body: For non-Grafana prom rules AlertRuleMenu calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` with `skipToken`, which becomes `undefined` in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. With undefined rule, `duplicateSupported` is true and Duplicate ability is `[true, hasGrafanaCreatePermission]`. OR-ing ruler and grafana Duplicate abilities then shows Duplicate for Mimir/Loki/cloud rules based on Grafana create permission instead of external write permission, exposing an action the user may not be allowed to perform on that datasource.

findings.title: Federated rule immutability check removed
findings.body: The old combined-rule abilities marked groups with `source_tenants` as federated via `isFederatedRuleGroup` and made them immutable. The new `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO. Mimir federated rule groups are read-only, but they will now appear editable and deletable in the UI, leading to failed API calls and attempts to modify rules that must not be edited.

findings.title: Provisioned check fails open when prom provenance missing
findings.body: `isProvisionedPromRule` returns true only if `promRule.provenance` is truthy, and `GrafanaRuleListItem` uses `Boolean(provenance)` for the provisioned badge. The PR adds `provenance` to the prom DTO without a backend change in the same diff. Any prom response without that field, stale cache, or recording rule without provenance evaluates to not-provisioned, so file-provisioned rules appear editable and lose their provisioned indicator, whereas the old ruler-based check used `grafana_alert.provenance`.

findings.title: Creating and deleting states silently dropped
findings.body: The old GrafanaGroupLoader matched ruler rules against prom rules to render Creating items for ruler-only rules and Deleting items for prom-only rules. The new loader renders only `promResponse.data.groups.at(0).rules`. Newly created rules not yet visible in Prometheus disappear from the list, and rules being deleted appear as normal actionable rules instead of a Deleting state, so users can act on stale rules and miss pending rules.

findings.title: Stale comment claims ruler preload still happens
findings.body: The cache-population block still comments that it preloads ruler rules to improve UX, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup')` call was removed. The comment is now wrong and will mislead future maintainers about what is cached and why initial load behaves as it does.
